page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-48 is a general-purpose server instance configured with 48 vCPUs and 192 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, featuring 24 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU allocation is dedicated, with cache sizes of 32 KB for L1d, 0.5 MB for L2, and 32 MB for L3. This configuration does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the n2d-standard-48 demonstrates strong CPU performance, placing in the top 25% for both single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, as well as the Passmark CPU suite. Cryptographic operations are highly efficient, with the Passmark CPU encryption test scoring in the top 25%, aided by hardware-accelerated AES and VAES instruction sets. Memory performance is also strong according to the Passmark memory score, though raw memory bandwidth tests for large blocks, both read and write, fall into the average category. For specialized tasks, the server achieves strong results in ray tracing, image processing, and text generation for small language models, while maintaining average performance in software compilation, database operations, and static web serving.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2d-standard-48 offers a balanced resource density suitable for workloads that require substantial multi-core processing power without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated tiers. The primary tradeoff is the complete absence of local NVMe storage and GPU hardware, meaning storage-heavy or deep-learning training tasks must rely on network-attached storage or alternative instance types. This server is best suited for general-purpose enterprise workloads, multi-threaded application servers, medium-scale web serving, software build pipelines, and moderate-scale text generation or LLM inference tasks.
